20: 呼啸山庄被描绘成一个阴暗压抑的地方，住在那里的人，后来的生活也愈发失序而艰难。小说中一些最富戏剧性的事件就发生在这里：例如，还是婴儿的哈里顿从楼梯栏杆上被扔下，却被希斯克利夫救住；凯瑟琳也曾在这里吐露她对希斯克利夫令人震惊的爱情。这里许多居民的人生都过早结束，疾病和苦难肆虐，不少人年纪轻轻便离开人世。例如，弗朗西丝·恩肖在产后死于肺结核，林顿·希斯克利夫则因体弱多病而早逝。

4: ‘呼啸山庄’是希斯克利夫先生住所的名字。‘呼啸’是一个重要的方言形容词，描述了它在暴风雨天气里所暴露的狂风骤雨。确实，那里四季都吹着清新刺骨的风：可以想象出北风刮过山崖边的力量，因为在房屋的尽头，有几株矮小的冷杉被吹得倾斜，还有一排瘦骨嶙峋的荆棘，所有枝条都朝一个方向伸展，仿佛在向太阳乞求温暖。

水流的奔涌声和磨坊的轰鸣声带来一种朦胧的沉寂，似乎让这片景色更显宁静。宽广的平原上，弗洛斯河在绿意葱茏的河岸间奔腾，奔向大海；温柔的潮汐急切地迎上去，以一种汹涌的拥抱将它挽留。

30.text: What is Setting?Definition + features: The setting is an integral part of the whole story (p.63). The overall setting of a narrative or dramatic work is the general locale, historical time and social circumstances (time/place/situation) in which its action occurs. (p.6/58)  Types: 1) fictional/imaginary setting vs. real setting 2) backdrop setting vs. integral setting (p.7) Significance:  1) Settings affect characters’ actions and feelings. It is often found that locations are used to provide clues to a character's mood or as a means of externalizing his or her inner turmoil [characterization] (p.63). 2) It helps readers to be engaged  in the story 3) develop the story plot Locale/Physical Location Historical TimeSocial Circumstances

31.text: How to develop setting?Giving the lay of the land   (actually describing topography and geography) is one way to introduce your setting, and it will work especially well if you intend for that land to play a vital role, almost as a character in its own right, in your story. 萨利内斯河谷位于加利福尼亚州北部。那是两条山脉之间的一片狭长的洼地，萨利内斯河蜿蜒曲折从中间流过，最后注入蒙特雷海湾。The Salinas Valley is in Northern California. It is a long narrow swale between two ranges of mountains, and the Salinas River winds and twists up the center until it falls at last into Monterey Bay.

33.text: How to develop setting?3. Displaying Sensory DetailsAnother way to introduce the setting is to appeal to the reader's five senses, paying special attention to what things look,  taste, smell, sound, and feel like. Warmth. Wind. Dancing blue waters, and the sound of waves. I see, hear, feel them all still. I even taste the sting of the salt against my lips, where the fine, misty spray coats them. And closer even than that, the lulling, drowsy smell of my mother‘s skin by my nose, where she holds me against her bosom, her hand making a sunshade across my forehead to shield my eyes. The boat is rocking gently, and my mother is rocking me as well, so I sway to a double rhythm. It makes me very sleepy, and the sloshing of the water all around me makes a blanket of sound, wrapping me securely. I am held safely, cradled in love and watchfulness. I remember. 34.text: Setting Vs. Sensory Details Using sensory detail is the key to bringing the setting alive. And it’s not about coming up with a few random sights, smells, sounds, or textures but about carefully choosing these elements via POV so that they not only bring a locale to life but share something helpful about the character experiencing the setting.Observing/ImaginingVisualizingDetailing

36.text: Definition:Transference is a psychological phenomenon, originally identified by Sigmund Freud, where a person unconsciously redirects or transfers feelings, desires, or attitudes from one person or situation in their past onto another person in the present. This typically occurs in therapeutic settings but can also happen in everyday relationships.  In literature/narrative writing, transference can be understood when we ‘take emotional meaning and transfer it onto people, places or things’  (p.60). By transferring emotions onto sensory elements, the writer can create layers of meaning that go beyond literal description, turning ordinary objects or events into powerful representations of internal states, conflicts, and themes.Transference

Displaying Concrete DetailsThe living room he took me into was neat, cozy, and plain: a large circular hooked rug, some slipcovered easy chairs, a worn sofa, a long wall of books, a piano, a phonograph, an oak library table systematically stacked with journals and magazines . .. Beyond the cushioned window seats and the colorless cotton curtains tied primly back I could see the bare limbs of big dark maple trees and fields of driven snow. Purity. Serenity. Simplicity. Seclusion. All one's concentration and flamboyance and originality reserved for the grueling, exalted, transcendent calling. 他带我进入了客厅，整洁舒适，大方朴素：一块巨型钩针圆地毯，几把带有沙发罩的安乐椅，一张陈旧的沙发，一个靠墙摆放的书架，一架钢琴，一架留声机，橡树书桌上有条不紊地堆放着报纸杂志……窗口的位置放着坐垫，纯色布窗帘系着，透过窗口，我看到黑色大枫树光秃秃的树枝和飘落在田野上的雪花。窗外纯洁无瑕、宁静安逸，房间简单朴素、与世隔绝。一切的灿烂奢华、新颖独到正是源于对疲惫夹杂着兴奋的呼唤。
